players.note: Patrick Mahomes broke out of his funk last week with 25.4 fantasy points (QB5 for the week). I didn't see that coming against Denver. It was Mahomes' first game with more than 17 fantasy points since Week 2. Overall, he is the QB14 in fantasy points per game. Mahomes continues to operate as a low aDOT machine. Among 30 qualifying passers, he is ninth in yards per attempt, fourth in passing success rate, and tenth in fantasy points per dropback, but he also has the highest rate of passing yards coming from yards after the catch (66.6%) and the lowest aDOT (6.11). Mahomes should have another QB1 outing this week against a struggling Jets pass defense. Over their last five games, New York has allowed the tenth-most yards per attempt, the fifth-highest passing success rate, the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, and the fifth-most fantasy points per dropback.

Since his Week 5 return, Jayden Daniels has been the QB5 in fantasy points per game. During those three games, he has averaged five rushing attempts and 45.3 yards on the ground (two rushing scores). Among 30 qualifying passers, Daniels is 20th in yards per attempt, 24th in passing success rate, 16th in catchable target rate, and 15th in highly accurate throw rate. Daniels will need a nice rushing performance this week to pay off for fantasy. The Rams pass defense has remained tough over their last five games, allowing the eighth-lowest EPA per dropback, the tenth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-lowest passing success rate, and the 14th-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

Matthew Stafford is the QB16 in fantasy points per game with four weeks with at least 18.5 fantasy points. Stafford has four 300-yard passing days this season and five games with multiple passing touchdowns. Among 30 qualifying passers, Stafford is 16th in yards per attempt, tenth in passing success rate, 20th in catchable target rate, and 23rd in hero throw rate. Washington has had some improvements over the last few weeks as a pass defense, but this is still just a middle-of-the-road pass defense. Over their last five games, Washington has allowed the third-highest CPOE while ranking 15th in passing success rate, 18th in EPA per dropback, and 16th in fantasy points per dropback. Stafford could easily post a nice QB1 day in Week 9.

Jordan Love is the QB10 in fantasy points per game. Love has multiple passing touchdowns in every game except one, while surpassing 280 passing yards in four games. Among 30 qualifying passers, Love is 14th in yards per attempt, 19th in passing success rate, first in deep ball rate, and 11th in hero throw rate. Love should have another QB1 outing this week. Over their last five games, New England has allowed the sixth-most yards per attempt, the eighth-highest passing success rate, and the seventh-most EPA per dropback.

Tyler Shough is the QB12 in fantasy points per game. Among 30 qualifying passers, Shough is 24th in yards per attempt, 17th in passing success rate, ninth in catchable target rate, and seventh in hero throw rate. The Saints rely on Shough's arm weekly to move the ball as their rushing offense has been non-existent. Shough (even after a bye week) is seventh in passing attempts and tenth in dropbacks. Shough will have a tough battle on hands this week. Over their last five games, Cleveland has allowed the ninth-fewest yards per attempt, the tenth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the fourth-lowest passing success rate, and the tenth-fewest EPA per dropback.

C.J. Stroud is the QB14 in fantasy points per game with three games this season with at least 20.9 fantasy points. Stroud could easily make that four after this week. Stroud has multiple passing touchdowns in four games this season and managed 300 passing yards three times. Among 30 qualifying passers, Stroud has been dealing, ranking 11th in yards per attempt, 14th in passing success rate, seventh in highly accurate throw rate, and first in hero throw rate. Over their last five games, the Bolts have been a middle-of-the-road pass defense, ranking 16th in yards per attempt, 13th in passing success rate, and 18th in CPOE.

Since Week 5, Malik Willis has been the QB7 in fantasy points per game. Last week, his production fell back to Earth as his rushing disappeared again. Willis ran only once with two yards. I simply don't understand why Miami isn't utilizing his legs and talents as a runner on a weekly basis, but at this point of the season his weekly volatility with his rushing will help or hurt his fantasy output. Willis has three games where he hasn't managed more than 12 rushing yards this season. Since Week 5, among 32 qualifying passers, we have seen growth as a passer as he has ranked 16th in yards per attempt, ninth in passing success rate, seventh in highly accurate throw rate, and 16th in catchable target rate. Willis could post another QB1 outing this week. Across their last five games, Detroit has allowed the 14th-most yards per attempt, the sixth-highest passing touchdown rate, the fourth-highest passing success rate, and the 12th-highest CPOE.

Kirk Cousins has been BALLING as the QB5 in fantasy points per game. Among 30 qualifying passers, Cousins is 12th in yards per attempt, eighth in passing success rate, 22nd in catchable target rate, and 18th in hero throw rate. Cousins is third in passing yards and second to only Joe Burrow in passing yards among all quarterbacks. Cousins has multiple passing touchdowns in every game this season except for one. This week, he gets a neutral matchup against the 49ers, who, over their last five games, have ranked 16th in passing success rate and EPA per dropback and have allowed the 14th-highest passing touchdown rate.

Over the last two weeks, Bo Nix has been the QB3 and QB12 in weekly scoring. Overall, he's the QB24 in fantasy points per game. I wish I could tell you that his level of play has massively improved, but that's not the case. Over the last two weeks, among 25 qualifying passers, Nix is 11th in yards per attempt and 12th in aDOT, but he is also 25th in passing success rate, 18th in highly accurate throw rate, and has the fifth-highest off-target rate. Yeah, it looks like more of the same from Nix. He could easily be a decent QB2 this week, but I wouldn't expect much more than that. Over their last five games, Carolina has been a middle-of-the-road matchup for passers, ranking 15th in fantasy points per dropback while giving up the tenth-highest CPOE and 12th-most EPA per dropback.

After posting 20 or more fantasy points in back-to-back games entering Week 8, Michael Penix managed to have a massive dud game against the Bucs. Penix completed only eight of 24 passes with four interceptions and 5.2 yards per attempt. It was an absolute nightmare fuel performance. With all that said, this is a good bounce-back spot for Penix. Overall, among 30 qualifying passers, Penix is tenth in yards per attempt, 15th in passing success rate, 27th in highly accurate throw rate, and he has the highest turnover-worthy throw rate. Over their last five games, Cincy has allowed the seventh-most yards per attempt, the ninth-highest passing touchdown rate, the sixth-highest passing success rate, and the 11th-most fantasy points per dropback. Penix could return to solid QB2 production this week.

Over the last two games, Bryce Young has looked more like last season's Young, as the QB24 and QB18 in weekly scoring. In those two games, among 25 qualifying passers, Young has ranked 24th in yards per attempt, 19th in highly accurate throw rate, 17th in catchable target rate, and 23rd in fantasy points per dropback. I don't think this is the week Young gets it back on track (if he does). Over their last five games, Denver has allowed the sixth-fewest yards per attempt, the 13th-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-fewest fantasy points per dropback, and the tenth-fewest EPA per dropback.

In his last two games of action for the Giants, J.J. McCarthy was the QB12 and QB23 in weekly fantasy scoring. The QB23 finish doesn't do his level of play justice. Among 40 qualifying passers, McCarthy is first in yards per attempt, first in aDOT, 17th in passing success rate, fourth in catchable target rate, and first in hero throw rate. The Eagles' pass defense has shown cracks in the pavement, and McCarthy can take advantage this week. Over the last five games, Philly has allowed the 12th-highest yards per attempt and the eighth-highest EPA per dropback, while ranking 17th in passing touchdown rate. During that span, Philly has also had issues with deep passing, giving up the tenth-highest passing success rate and the third-most deep passing yards. Among those 40 qualifying passers, McCarthy is first in deep ball rate by a mile with 18.4%. The Eagles have also had the third-lowest pressure rate and the second-lowest quick pressure rate in that span. Chef McCarthy should have time in the kitchen to cook again this week.

With Sam Darnold sidelined with a quad injury, Drew Lock will make a start for Seattle. Funny enough, his last start of the season was against the Cardinals. In that game, he completed 73.1% of his passes with 235 yards through the air and three passing scores. Lock was the QB9 in weekly scoring that week. This season, among 40 qualifying passers, Lock is third in yards per attempt, seventh in highly accurate throw rate, 22nd in catchable target rate, and 11th in hero throw rate. Lock could have another QB1-level stat line this week. Arizona's pass defense has been horrible. Over their last five games, the Cards have allowed the ninth-most yards per attempt, the fifth-highest passing touchdown rate, the sixth-most EPA per dropback, and the second-most fantasy points per dropback.

Since his return to the lineup, Baker Mayfield has averaged only seven passing attempts and 32 passing yards per game. Yes, I know the weather was a factor in one of those games, but Mayfield hasn't been good with the passing attempts he has had since his return. Since Week 7, he has had only 4.5 yards per attempt, a 6.58 aDOT, and a 42.9% highly accurate throw rate. I expect him to pass more out of necessity this week, but I also expect the Bucs to hide him as much as possible. Sit Mayfield and fade this passing attack overall.

Carson Wentz will draw the start for Minnesota this week. In Wentz's two games of action this season, he was the QB12 and QB30 in weekly scoring. Among 42 qualifying passers this season, Wentz is 20th in yards per attempt, 37th in passing success rate, 40th in highly accurate throw rate, and 37th in catchable target rate. Wentz likely isn't the savior for this offense and passing attack. His accuracy issues have been substantial. The thing working in Wentz's favor is the fact that the Bills' pass defense hasn't been a unit to be scared of this season. Over their last five games, Buffalo has allowed the 13th-highest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-highest passing success rate, the 13th-most EPA per dropback, and the 15th-most fantasy points per dropback. Wentz can post serviceable QB2 numbers this week.

Daniel Jones is the QB37 in fantasy points per game. Just let that soak in for a second. He has managed more than 13 fantasy points only once this season. It has been a spectacular struggle bus for Jones and the Colts' offense. Among 30 qualifying passers, Jones is 29th in yards per attempt, 21st in passing success rate, 25th in highly accurate throw rate, and dead last in hero throw rate. I don't have any faith in Jones at all, but maybe Dallas can allow him to post a decent stat line this week. Over their last five games, Dallas has allowed the 11th-most yards per attempt, the 14th-highest passer rating, the eighth-highest CPOE, and the tenth-most EPA per dropback.

I don't see a reason for hope for Justin Herbert at this point. He hasn't passed for more than 260 yards in any game this season. Herbert has zero games with multiple passing touchdowns, and he has thrown an interception in every game this season. Herbert is QB34 in fantasy points per game with zero games with 15 or more fantasy points. I need a prove-it game before I'm willing to plug him into any fantasy lineup.

After last week's QB13 finish, Geno Smith is the QB20 in fantasy points per game with three games of at least 19 fantasy points under his belt. Among 30 qualifying passers, Smith is sixth in yards per attempt, 11th in passing success rate, 14th in highly accurate throw rate, and fifth in catchable target rate. Smith has been a very good streaming option when the matchup has presented itself. Well, the matchup is horrible this week. Sit Smith. Across their last five games, Kansas City has allowed the fifth-lowest passing touchdown rate and passing success rate, the 14th-fewest yards per attempt, and the 11th-fewest fantasy points per dropback.

With Deshaun Watson dealing with a concussion, Shedeur Sanders will be the starting quarterback for the Browns this week. Last year, in Weeks 12-18, with Sanders starting, he was a QB1 in weekly scoring only once. Last year, among 38 qualifying passers, Sanders was 30th in yards per attempt, 37th in passing success rate, and 23rd in hero throw rate. Yes, I know there's not much to be positive about in that sample, but we did see flashes from Sanders with a 364 passing yard outing (three passing scores) against the Titans. Sanders also had at least 20 rushing yards in each of his final five games last year, so there's some rushing production here to chew on. Last year, it was tough to evaluate Sanders behind a patchwork offensive line and with only Harold Fannin to throw to as a serviceable pass catcher at times. Sanders has a rebuilt offensive line to operate behind this season and plenty of skill talent around him. The Saints' pass defense has been horrible. Sanders should post solid QB2 numbers this week, and I wouldn't be surprised if he flirted with low-end QB1 production. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most yards per attempt, the 11th-highest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-highest passing success rate, and the tenth-most fantasy points per dropback.

Tanner McKee has been benched. Joe Milton will now be the starting quarterback for the Eagles. We'll see if he can hold the job for the rest of the season. Since 2024, Milton has only had 57 regular-season dropbacks to work with as a sample size. With those dropbacks, Milton has had 8.1 yards per attempt, a 53.8% passing success rate, a 13.5% deep ball rate, an 80.9% catchable target rate, and a 5.8% hero throw rate. Those are all solid, if not STRONG, numbers. Again, this is an incredibly small sample, but it at least paints a picture of optimism, which I don't think we can say existed for McKee after what we've seen this season. This week, he'll have a tough matchup against the Giants, but he could still return serviceable QB2 production. Over their last five games, the Giants have allowed the second-fewest yards per attempt, the third-lowest passing success rate, the seventh-lowest CPOE, and the sixth-lowest EPA per dropback.

Last week, Gardner Minshew was a JJ McCarthy-level hero. He led the Cards to a win against Dallas after taking over for Jacoby Brissett. He completed 17 of 23 passes with 188 passing yards (8.2 yards per attempt) and three scores. I love the mustache maestro, but he comes crashing back to Earth this week against Seattle. Over their last five games, Seattle has allowed the fourth-fewest yards per attempt and fantasy points per dropback, the sixth-lowest passing success rate, and the fifth-fewest EPA per dropback. Minshew will have streamable weeks, but this isn't one of them.

Baltimore's third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano will be starting this week for the Ravens. Last week, with injuries to Tyler Huntley and Lamar Jackson, he was pressed into duty. The team just traded for Jacoby Brissett, but he won't have enough time to take the starting job this week. He finished with 21 passing attempts, a 47.6% completion rate, 91 passing yards (one pick), and 4.3 yards per attempt. This preseason, he had some success. Among 62 qualifying passers, he was 22nd in yards per attempt and ninth in adjusted completion rate with a 3:1 passing touchdown-to-interception ratio. Fagnano also had the tenth-lowest aDOT. If he can even be a league-average game manager this week, it should be considered a win for Baltimore. Adding to all of this, he is playing through an ankle injury. He's a low-end QB2 with a rough matchup. Over their last five games, the Jags have allowed the eighth-lowest passing touchdown rate, the 12th-lowest passing success rate, and the seventh-lowest EPA per dropback.

Deshaun Watson is the QB22 in fantasy points per game. He has added 6.4 rushing attempts and 27.1 rushing yards per game to his weekly fantasy floor and ceiling. Among 30 qualifying passers, he is 14th in yards per attempt, 12th in passing success rate, tenth in highly accurate throw rate, and 18th in catchable target rate. Watson should post solid QB2 numbers this week with the upside to be a low-end QB1. Over their last five games, New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most yards per attempt, the 11th-highest passing touchdown rate, the seventh-highest passing success rate, and the tenth-most fantasy points per dropback. Watson has been placed in the concussion protocol this week. It's possible that Watson might not start this week. I'll update his outlook on Friday. Shedeur Sanders could be starting for Cleveland this week.
